records.central_bank: Banque de la République du Burundi
records.years: Governor of the central bank 1992-1998; sitting on Interbank Burundi's board at 31 December 2022 and still at 14 March 2025
records.move: Governor, Banque de la République du Burundi (1992-1998), later a member of the board of directors of Interbank Burundi SA, chairing its audit committee (2022) and its credit committee (2025)
records.summary: Mathias Sinamenye ran Burundi's central bank, the Banque de la République du Burundi, from 1992 to 1998. Interbank Burundi's own 2022 annual report lists him on the bank's board of directors as 'Mathias Sinamenye, Président du Comité d'Audit', the director who chairs the committee overseeing the bank's audits; the bank's 2024 annual report still lists him on the board, as 'Président du Comité Crédit', the committee that oversees lending. The same 2022 annual report states who owns the bank: 'L'actionnariat est, depuis le début, totalement privé' (the shareholding has been entirely private from the start), made up of 'Burundais et d'étrangers, résidents et non résidents, de plus de dix nationalités, avec participation des salariés', and the report calls Interbank 'une des pionnières dans le domaine des banques privées au Burundi' (one of the pioneers among private banks in Burundi). So the same person held the top job at the public central bank and then sat on the board of a bank the bank itself describes as wholly privately held.
records.source_title: Interbank Burundi SA, Rapport annuel 2022 (Conseil d'administration listing and Actionnariat section); governorship dates from Wikipedia, 'Mathias Sinamenye'

records.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus
records.people: Deputy Head of Department, National Bank of the Republic of Belarus (1998-2005), afterwards in senior roles at Priorbank (2005-2016)
records.move: from Deputy Head of Department at the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus (1998-2005) to Priorbank (Raiffeisen Group), 2005-2016, in roles including Head of the Project Management Office, Chief Digital Officer and Head of Retail Banking
records.summary: A career page published by Ipoteka Bank sets out an unbroken record: 1998 to 2005 at the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus, finishing as Deputy Head of Department, then 2005 to 2016 at Priorbank, listed on that page as part of the Raiffeisen Group, in roles including Head of the Project Management Office, Chief Digital Officer and Head of Retail Banking, then 2016 to 2023 at Dabrabyt Bank. Who owns Priorbank is stated by a separate report on the bank's sale, which calls Priorbank 'the largest private bank in Belarus' and says that '87.74% of shares in Priorbank OJSC will be transferred to SOVEN 1', the 87.74% stake having been held until then through a subsidiary of the Austrian group Raiffeisen Bank International AG. The central bank role here was below senior management, so the role is given and the name is not.

records.people: Farhat Bengdara (Deputy Governor, then Governor of the Central Bank of Libya, 2006-2011)
records.move: held the governorship of the Central Bank of Libya (2006-2011) and a seat on the board of UniCredit SpA as board member and vice-chairman from 29 April 2009 at the same time
records.summary: Farhat Bengdara was Deputy Governor and then Governor of the Central Bank of Libya from 2006 to 2011, and from 29 April 2009 he sat on the board of UniCredit SpA as board member and vice-chairman, so the two roles overlapped. UniCredit's own shareholder-structure page sets out who holds the shares: Aabar Luxembourg S.A.R.L. 5.039%, BlackRock Inc. 4.993% in non-discretional asset management, Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio Verona, Vicenza, Belluno e Ancona 3.460%, Central Bank of Libya 2.923% and Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino 2.517%. That table is mixed: most of the named holders are private investors and foundations, and one, the Central Bank of Libya itself, is a state body. The career list comes from a Wikipedia article, so the source is marked weak.
records.status: concurrent private and central bank role, no finding

records.people: Teotónio Jaime dos Anjos Comiche (head of the accounting department of the Banco de Moçambique 1976-1983, director of accounting 1983-1989, member of its board of administration 1989-1992)
records.move: from member of the board of administration of the Banco de Moçambique (1989-1992) to executive director of Banco Comercial de Moçambique, S.A. (1992-2000), then executive director of Banco Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. / Millennium bim (2000-2015), then chair of the general meeting of Seguradora Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. (2016-2021)
records.summary: Millennium bim publishes his dated CV. It lists him at the Banco de Moçambique (Banco Central) from 1976 to 1992, ending as a member of its board of administration 1989-1992, then as executive director of Banco Comercial de Moçambique, S.A. from 1992 to 2000 and of Banco Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. from 2000 to 2015, then at the insurer Seguradora Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. from 2015 to 2021. On the ownership of the bank he joined in 2000, the Institute of Developing Economies company file for Mozambique sets out the holdings in Millennium BIM as '66.69% BCP Internacional II, Sociedade Unipessoal, SGPS', '17.76% Estado Moçambicano', '4.95% INSS - Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social', '4.15% EMOSE - Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros, SARL', '1.08% FDC - Fundação para o Desenvolvimento da Comunidade' and '5.37% Gestores, Técnicos e Trabalhadores', and describes the parent Banco Comercial Português as 'a Portugal-based, privately owned bank'. So the holding is mixed and the majority holder is stated to be private. Millennium bim's own 2008 annual report prints the same shareholder table during his time there: 'BCP Internacional II, SGPS, Lda. 4.941.393 66,69%', 'Estado Moçambicano 1.271.440 17,16%', 'INSS - Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social 366.846 4,95%', 'EMOSE - Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros, S.A.R.L. 307.319 4,15%'.
